newsitem.title: CHILE: Edelnor rules out Gas Atacama deal.
newsitem.headline: Edelnor rules out Gas Atacama deal.

text.p: Chilean power utility Edelnor said it has decided not to sign up with the Gas Atacama natural gas pipeline project which plans to bring gas across the Andes from Salta in northern Argentina.
Gas Atacama is owned by Chilean electricity giant Endesa and U.S. firm CMS Energy.
"After analyzing the final terms of the contract proposed by the Gas Atacama pipeline...we consider (the deal) is not in the best interest of Edelor," said general manager Mark Lynch.
The announcement opens the way to deal with two other gas-linked projects which are also jostling for customers.
"Edelnor believes that in the near future other alternatives will emerge...which will represent a better opportunity for the company and the energy system in the north," said Lynch.
Edelnor, one of the largest generators in northern Chile, is around 65 percent owned by Southern Co.
The company's statement came after the closing deadline for potential customers interested in signing up.
Recently privatized utility Tocopilla announced last week that it plans to build a natural gas pipeline from Argentina to the port of Tocopilla, which lies north of Antofagasta.
The company will start asking interested clients to sign up to the project from March 17.
A third group led by generator Chilgener is planning to build gas-fired power plants in Argentina and bring the electricity to Chile using a transmission line across the Andes.
All the companies are attracted by the huge energy demands created by the rapid growth of the copper and gold mining industry in Chile's arid north.
